First, let's go to the North Hemisphere, where we live. In the North Hemisphere, we are at a certain point in the year where the sun is high in the sky. When the sun is high in the sky, it heats up the Earth more than when it is low in the sky. This makes the air near the Earth warm and dry.

As the warm air near the Earth rises, it forms clouds and precipitation (waterfall or rain) near the Earth. This is why we have spring and summer. The warm air near the Earth is also why we have warm temperatures and sunshine during these seasons.

Now, let's go to the South Hemisphere, where we live. In the South Hemisphere, we are at a certain point in the year where the sun is low in the sky. When the sun is low in the sky, it heats up the Earth less than when it is high in the sky. This makes the air near the Earth warm and dry.

As the warm air near the Earth rises, it forms clouds and precipitation (waterfall or rain) near the Earth. This is why we have autumn (fall) and winter. The warm air near the Earth is also why we have warm temperatures and sunshine during these seasons.

So, you can see why we have seasons.
